summary: Streaming chat sessions disconnect or stall mid-generation (SSE/WebSocket) after recent latency regression
description:
Issue summary: Multiple enterprise customers report streaming chat sessions disconnecting or stalling mid-generation when using SSE or WebSocket streaming endpoints. Frequency increased starting ~2026-03-01 after a runtime rollout.

Impact: Customers observe partial responses (stream stops) or sudden socket closures. Visible in real traffic and reproducible with load tests for longer generations (>800 tokens). Affects interactive chat features and can cause broken UX and retry storms.

Environment: Production. Primarily observed in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Affects both hosted API and Dedicated nodes running the serving-runtime v3.2.1 rollout.

Observed client symptoms:
- SSE streams stop emitting events mid-generation (no final chunk) and client shows stalled spinner.
- WebSocket sessions receive connection closed by server (RST/EOF) after 10-30s of inactivity.
- Some customers see 502/504 proxied errors before disconnect.

Relevant logs/metrics:
- Elevated 95th and 99th p99 latency for token generation since 2026-03-01 02:00 UTC in us-east.
- Spike in kernel queue wait times and GPU scheduler queue depth on a subset of nodes.
- Proxy (api-gateway) shows increased upstream reset_count and stream timeouts.
- Sentry errors: "streaming: client EOF" and "upstream reset while streaming" tied to same timeframe.

References: Sentry: SENTRY-31022, Grafana dashboard: /d/latency/streaming-latency, Slack thread: #support (thread TS: 2026-03-01T08:12Z).
steps_to_reproduce: Open an SSE or WebSocket streaming session against /v1/chat/stream with model redwood/open-llama-13b-v1
Send a prompt that triggers a long generation (>800 tokens) or includes complex decode loops
Observe stream for 30-60s; note if events stop before final end-of-stream or connection closes unexpectedly
Run the same test against a staging cluster (serving-runtime v3.2.0) to compare behavior

investigation_notes:
Timeline: Regression appeared after serving-runtime v3.2.1 rollout on 2026-03-01. Initial telemetry points to two correlated issues: (1) a kernel-selection change that increases per-token latency for certain attention patterns, raising request duration beyond proxy idle timeout thresholds; (2) intermittent KV cache thrashing on particular model workloads leading to scheduler queueing.

Evidence collected:
- Profiling traces show a 2.1x increase in per-token compute time at 95th percentile on affected nodes.
- Gateway logs show upstream reset_count peaks that align with token latency spikes.
- Canary rollback to kernel selector v3.2.0 reduces streaming abort rate by ~85% during controlled tests.

Next steps:
- Patch: revert the kernel-selection change for streaming path and ship v3.2.2 with fallback to the previous kernel selector for long-generation requests.
- Autoscaler: add emergency capacity headroom for streaming-heavy pods to avoid queue buildup.
- Cache: tune KV cache retention policy to reduce eviction spikes; add targeted metric to detect thrash.
- Communication: send customer-facing update and an RCA postmortem after full fix.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: traffic from affected customers routed to a canary pool running serving-runtime with previous kernel selector (v3.2.0) while eng prepares v3.2.2 with kernel fallback. Early validation from AcmeDocs reports stable streams for previously failing prompts.

Permanent fix plan: ship v3.2.2 that reintroduces the older kernel path for streaming and includes KV cache tuning. Schedule postmortem and update runbook to include steps for rolling back kernel selector and verifying streaming health.

Follow-ups: INT-4023 assigned to Eng for root-cause and PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1284 tracks the v3.2.2 changes.
notes: Customer requested a formal RCA and timeline. CS updated SLO credits as a temporary measure pending final resolution.
